text:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT triggered — elevated 5xx error rate observed for egress cluster LAX2 (region: northamerica-west1). Alert group: egress-pathes. Paging infra-oncall.
amelia: seeing spikes in 5xx from LAX2 too. Customer reports starting ~11:12 UTC. Error rate ~12% on generation requests, latency up as well. tl;dr: some egress peers failing, causing retries + queueing.
sanjay: confirmed. Top symptom: outbound NAT to external peering is dropping connections intermittently. Affected: hosted API customers in US-West, some Dedicated pools routing via LAX2. Initial trigger: BGP flap with upstream provider according to border logs.
infra-oncall: oncall here (amelia tagged me). I'm taking lead. Has anyone started a status page entry yet?
ops-bot: draft status page entry ready: 

```
Title: Partial egress outage impacting US-West (LAX2) — degraded API responses
Impact: Some requests may return 5xx or experience increased latency. A subset of customers behind LAX2 egress are affected.
ETA: Investigating — next update in 30 minutes.
```
kate: Please don't publish until we have mitigation steps and clear scope. We should call out Dedicated vs Hosted differences.
amelia: agree. I'll gather scope. Quick note: Dedicated pools using reserved LAX2 egress via peering are >80% of the errors, but some Hosted traffic via global router also impacted (fallbacks attempted, causing load elsewhere).
sanjay: adding logs snippet from border router (redacted): 
```
May 14 11:13:02 lr-border1 kernel: conntrack: table full, dropping packet
May 14 11:13:05 bgp-daemon[2213]: neighbor 203.0.113.5 reset (flap)
```
infra-oncall: immediate mitigation idea: 1) advertise alternate egress via LAX1/SEA1 (BGP prep) 2) temporarily shift global router policy to prefer west-us2 fallback pool for requests tagged with customer-tier != enterprise. Can we push that safely? @jamal any concerns on burst capacity?
jamal: we can shift the route weight quickly. Execute with canary: update route for 5% traffic first, monitor CPU/gpu queue. Command to adjust weights on the global router controller: 

```
# set weight for LAX2 -> 90, LAX1 -> 5, WEST-US2 -> 5
rctl set route-weight --cluster LAX2=90 --cluster LAX1=5 --cluster WEST-US2=5
```
jamal: to do the canary run: 

```
rctl set canary --route egress-west --percent 5
# watch metrics: /dash/egress/latency and /dash/egress/5xx
```
ops-bot: recommended monitoring hooks: add alert if 5xx > 3% on fallback pools or if queue depth increases > 2000. I can apply temporary thresholds.
amelia: I'm going to post a provisional internal comms update for SRE/Support. Draft below — please annotate: 

"We are investigating elevated 5xx rates impacting the LAX2 egress cluster (northamerica-west1). Root cause appears to be an upstream peering instability causing connection drops. Current action: infra-oncall performing traffic reroute canary to LAX1/WEST-US2, monitoring for customer impact. Impacted: Hosted API users and some Dedicated pools in US-West. Next update in 15-30 minutes. POCs: infra-oncall (infra-oncall), network eng (sanjay)."

kate: good. Add: links to support KB + guidance for customers to retry with exponential backoff (we shouldn't leak internal routing details). Also prepare targeted customer DM for affected Dedicated accounts.
product-ops: I can draft a customer-facing blurb for status page when you give scope: something short like: 

"We are investigating intermittent errors in US-West. If you're experiencing failures, we recommend retrying requests; we're working on a fix and will update soon."

infra-oncall: canary started at 11:18 UTC (rctl canary 5%). Monitoring now. Early signal: 5xx on canary path 0.6% -> looks ok. However LAX2 still seeing backpressure in other pods.
sanjay: started coordination with upstream provider — they've acknowledged a BGP flap and are applying suppress of route churn. Could take 10–20 mins to stabilize.
jamal: increasing canary to 20% in 3 minutes to relieve LAX2. Command executed. Watch for GPU queue rise on WEST-US2. Notify me if per-node CPU > 75%.
ops-bot: alert thresholds temporarily applied. I'll also create a ticket to follow up on postmortem playbooks once service stabilizes.
amelia: updating internal channel with current state and next steps. Will hold off public status page publish until we validate 20% canary behavior for 5 minutes.
kate: once we confirm, publish the status page entry including: affected region, recommended customer action (retry/backoff), and ETA for next update. Keep it high-level.
product-ops: drafted status page message ready-to-paste when approved.
infra-oncall: canary at 20% shows reduced 5xx for customers routed off LAX2. Still some backlog but trending down. Upstream reports stabilization window ~+10m.
sanjay: marking affected clusters list: LAX2-egress-poolA, LAX2-egress-poolB, routed Dedicated instances with explicit egress via LAX2. If we need to contact Dedicated customers directly, product-ops + Kate please prepare targeted emails.
kate: I'll queue targeted notify for 6 customers that have reserved LAX2 egress — will include mitigation steps and an apology. Template: 

"We experienced intermittent network instability affecting LAX2 egress. This may have caused increased errors for traffic routed via LAX2. Our on-call team has shifted traffic and the upstream provider is applying fixes. We will follow up with a root cause and timeline."

amelia: planning to close loop: once upstream confirms route stable and our 5xx rates <1% for 10 minutes, we'll: 1) revert temporary route weights back to normal 2) publish post-incident note in #postmortems 3) create RCA ticket.
ops-bot: notation: incident severity: Sev3 (partial degradation) — escalate to Sev2 if >10% customers impacted or >20% 5xx sustained.
product-ops: go ahead and publish the status page now (I think we have safe wording). Approved by infra-oncall and kate.
ops-bot: status page update posted at 11:36 UTC: "Investigating — Partial egress outage impacting US-West (LAX2). A subset of customers may see errors; mitigation in progress. Next update in 30 minutes." :bell:
jamal: upstream confirms route stable at 11:40 UTC. We begin shift back: 
```
rctl set route-weight --cluster LAX2=95 --cluster LAX1=3 --cluster WEST-US2=2
rctl set canary --route egress-west --percent 0
```
infra-oncall: rolling back canary now. Monitoring for regressions.
sanjay: 5xx dropped to 0.8% cluster-wide, latency normalized. Good to start closing.
kate: published customer-facing incident note to affected Dedicated accounts at 11:52 UTC. Included contact for support and ETA for RCA.
amelia: final internal note: incident resolved at 11:53 UTC. Follow-up actions: postmortem, add additional guardrails for conntrack table, review BGP neighbor timers with upstream. Thanks everyone. :tada:
product-ops: filing post-incident communication to be posted in #postmortems with timeline and action items.
jamal: I'll own immediate mitigation playbook updates. Add me to RCA ticket.
sanjay: adding network-side runbook changes. Will propose config: increase conntrack table size + BGP dampening for that peer.
amelia: good work. Closing thread.
